transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That stuttering on and off is probably the vacuum's safety system kicking in because it can't get enough air. It’s not usually a motor fault at this stage. Please check these two common causes:
1. Filters: If you’ve washed them recently, are they completely dry? A filter that is even slightly damp will cause pulsing. They need 24 hours to dry fully in a warm room.
2. Blockages: Detach the wand and floorhead from the main body. Look through each part to make sure nothing (like a coin or clump of dust) is stuck inside. Also, if your model has a motorised brush bar on the floorhead, turn it over and check that hair or thread isn’t tangled around the roller, preventing it from spinning freely. Let me know what you find with the filters and airways.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. never washed the filter tho, didnt know u could. ill check the wand n head now

Good to know it's a V8 Animal. Since the battery is full, that stuttering sound is probably the vacuum cutting power because airflow is blocked—it’s protecting itself from overheating. Please go ahead and check the wand and floorhead as planned. Once you've checked those parts: did you find a blockage, and does it run steadily now?
found a big clump of hair n cat litter stuck at the bottom of the wand where the head goes on, pulled it out. its running proper now, good suction no pulsin

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That’s excellent news. It was just the safety system kicking in because of that blockage—nothing broken there. To stop it happening again, try to give the wand and floorhead a quick check every now and then, especially since you have cats (hair and litter are the usual culprits). Also, if you ever do wash the filters, make sure they are 100% dry before putting them back in. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
